ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure is square ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right; F is located on the right side CD; the line segment from B to F passes through the interior of the square and intersects diagonal AC at E; the figure also draws line segment DE. Then reason: because E is on BF, the known ∠CBF=20° is also ∠CBE=20°. In the square, ∠ABC=90°, therefore ∠ABE=90°−20°=70°. Also because AC is the diagonal of the square, E is on AC, so ∠BAE=45°. In triangle ABE, ∠AEB=180°−70°−45°=65°. The problem gives △ABE ≅ △ADE, according to the corresponding vertices E corresponds to E, so ∠AED=∠AEB=65°.
